topics: Law of Sines, Law of Cosines & Heron's formula

body.en: Advanced Euclidean geometry represents roughly 10% of the EST II Math Level 1 exam. Candidates must master rigorous angle relationships with parallel lines and transversals, prove and apply triangle similarity and congruence criteria, apply the Law of Cosines and Law of Sines to non-right (oblique) triangles, compute areas using sine-area and Heron's formulas, and analyze regular polygon apothems and diagonals.

label.en: Definition 4.1 — Transversals, Similarity, and Polygon Properties

body.en:
Core geometric definitions and structural angle relationships:
  • Parallel Lines and Transversals: Two parallel lines intersected by a transversal produce equal alternate interior, alternate exterior, and corresponding angles; consecutive interior angles are supplementary (sum to \(180^\circ\)).
  • Triangle Similarity & Congruence Criteria:
    1. Congruence (\(\cong\)): SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, and HL (Hypotenuse-Leg for right triangles). All corresponding sides and angles are equal.
    2. Similarity (\(\sim\)): AA (Angle-Angle), SAS similarity, and SSS similarity. Corresponding angles are equal; corresponding sides are in constant ratio \(k\).
  • Polygon Formulas: For a convex polygon with \(n\) vertices:
    1. Interior angle sum: \(S_{\text{int}} = (n - 2) \times 180^\circ\).
    2. Each interior angle of a regular \(n\)-gon: \(\theta_{\text{int}} = \frac{(n - 2) \times 180^\circ}{n} = 180^\circ - \frac{360^\circ}{n}\).
    3. Exterior angle sum: \(S_{\text{ext}} = 360^\circ\) (each exterior angle is \(\frac{360^\circ}{n}\)).
    4. Number of distinct diagonals: \(D = \frac{n(n - 3)}{2}\).
    5. Area of a regular polygon: \(A = \frac{1}{2} a P\), where \(a\) is the apothem and \(P\) is the perimeter.

label.en: Theorem 4.1 — Exterior Angle Theorem, Law of Cosines, and Heron's Formula

body.en:
Fundamental theorems for general triangles and polygon mensuration:
  • Exterior Angle Theorem: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent (remote) interior angles:
    \[ \theta_{\text{ext}} = \angle A + \angle B \]
  • Triangle Inequality Theorem: In any non-degenerate triangle with side lengths \(a, b, c\):
    \[ |a - b| < c < a + b \]
  • Law of Cosines (for any oblique triangle):
    \[ c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab \cos C \implies \cos C = \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab} \]
  • Heron's Formula: For a triangle with side lengths \(a, b, c\) and semi-perimeter \(s = \frac{a + b + c}{2}\):
    \[ \text{Area} = \sqrt{s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)} \]

label.en: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — Triangles, Polygons & Area

body.en:
• Linear vs. Area vs. Volume Scale Factors: If two similar polygons have a linear scale factor of \(k\), their perimeters scale by \(k\), but their areas scale by \(k^2\). On EST II, questions often provide the ratio of areas (e.g. \(9:16\)) and ask for perimeter — take the square root (\(3:4\)) first!
  • Regular Polygon Angle Inversions: Interior angle is \(\frac{(n-2)180°}{n}\), while exterior angle is \(\frac{360°}{n}\). Notice that \(\text{interior} + \text{exterior} = 180°\). It is almost always faster to compute the exterior angle first and subtract from \(180°\).
  • Triangle Inequality Theorem: For any valid triangle with sides \(a, b, c\), the sum of any two sides must be strictly greater than the third: \(a + b > c\), \(a + c > b\), \(b + c > a\). This implies \(|a - b| < c < a + b\).
  • Heron's Formula vs. Trigonometric Area: If all 3 sides are known, use Heron's formula: \(A = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}\) where semi-perimeter \(s = \frac{a+b+c}{2}\). If two sides and included angle are known, use \(\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C\).

label.en: Worked Example 4.A — Oblique Triangle Solution via Law of Cosines

body.en:
In triangle \(ABC\), side \(a = 7\text{ cm}\), side \(b = 10\text{ cm}\), and included angle \(C = 60^\circ\).
(a) Find the exact length of side \(c\).
(b) Calculate the exact area of triangle \(ABC\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Apply the Law of Cosines:
    \[ c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab \cos C \]
    Substitute values with \(\cos 60^\circ = 0.5\):
    \[ c^2 = 7^2 + 10^2 - 2(7)(10)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 49 + 100 - 70 = 79 \]
    Taking the square root gives:
    \[ c = \mathbf{\sqrt{79}\text{ cm}} \approx 8.89\text{ cm} \]
  2. (b) Calculate the area using sine formula:
    \[ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} a b \sin C = \frac{1}{2}(7)(10)\sin(60^\circ) = 35 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \mathbf{\frac{35\sqrt{3}}{2}\text{ cm}^2} \approx 30.31\text{ cm}^2 \]

label.en: Worked Example 4.B — Regular Polygon Apothem & Area Analysis

body.en:
A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius \(R = 8\text{ cm}\).
(a) Determine the apothem \(a\) of the hexagon.
(b) Compute the exact area of the hexagon.
(c) Calculate the exact area of the region inside the circle but outside the hexagon.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Find side length and apothem:
    In a regular hexagon, side length equals circumradius: \(s = R = 8\text{ cm}\).
    The apothem is the height of an equilateral triangle with side length 8:
    \[ a = s \cos(30^\circ) = 8 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \mathbf{4\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}} \]
  2. (b) Compute hexagon area:
    Perimeter is \(P = 6 \times 8 = 48\text{ cm}\):
    \[ A_{\text{hex}} = \frac{1}{2} a P = \frac{1}{2}(4\sqrt{3})(48) = \mathbf{96\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2} \approx 166.28\text{ cm}^2 \]
  3. (c) Shaded region area:
    Area of circle is \(A_{\text{circle}} = \pi R^2 = \pi (8^2) = 64\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
    \[ A_{\text{region}} = A_{\text{circle}} - A_{\text{hex}} = \mathbf{64\pi - 96\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2} \approx 34.78\text{ cm}^2 \]

label.en: Worked Example 4.C — Triangle Inequality & Integer Side Constraints

body.en:
Two sides of an obtuse triangle have lengths 6 and 9. If the third side \(x\) is an integer, determine the number of possible values for \(x\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Apply the Triangle Inequality Theorem:
    For any triangle with sides 6, 9, and \(x\):
    \[ |9 - 6| < x < 9 + 6 \implies 3 < x < 15 \]
  2. Apply the Obtuse Triangle Criteria:
    A triangle is obtuse if \(c^2 > a^2 + b^2\) where \(c\) is the longest side:
    Case 1: 9 is the longest side (\(x \le 9\)):
    \[ 9^2 > 6^2 + x^2 \implies 81 > 36 + x^2 \implies x^2 < 45 \implies x < \sqrt{45} \approx 6.71 \]
    Integer values satisfying \(3 < x < 6.71\) are \(x = 4, 5, 6\).
    Case 2: \(x\) is the longest side (\(x > 9\)):
    \[ x^2 > 6^2 + 9^2 = 36 + 81 = 117 \implies x > \sqrt{117} \approx 10.82 \]
    Integer values satisfying \(10.82 < x < 15\) are \(x = 11, 12, 13, 14\).
  3. Combine valid integer values:
    Possible values of \(x\) are \(\{4, 5, 6, 11, 12, 13, 14\}\).
    There are exactly 7 possible integer values.

question.en: Two sides of a right triangle are 7 cm and 10 cm. If the third side is the hypotenuse, find: (a) the exact hypotenuse length, and (b) the measure of the smaller acute angle to the nearest tenth of a degree.

solution.en:
(a) Exact hypotenuse: \[ c = \sqrt{7^2 + 10^2} = \sqrt{49 + 100} = \mathbf{\sqrt{149}\text{ cm}} \approx 12.21\text{ cm}. \]

(b) Smaller acute angle: The smaller angle is opposite the shorter leg (7 cm): \[ \tan\theta = \frac{7}{10} = 0.7 \implies \theta = \arctan(0.7) \approx \mathbf{35.0^\circ}. \]

question.en: A regular hexagon has side length \(s = 6\text{ cm}\). (a) Calculate the exact area of the hexagon. (b) Find the length of the long diagonal connecting two opposite vertices.

solution.en:
(a) Exact area: A regular hexagon is composed of 6 congruent equilateral triangles of side length \(s = 6\). The area of one equilateral triangle is \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2 = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(36) = 9\sqrt{3}\). Total area is: \[ A = 6 \times 9\sqrt{3} = \mathbf{54\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2} \approx 93.53\text{ cm}^2. \]

(b) Long diagonal: The long diagonal passes through the center of the circumscribed circle and equals twice the side length: \[ d = 2s = 2(6) = \mathbf{12\text{ cm}}. \]

question.en: In triangle \(PQR\), side \(p = 8\), side \(q = 11\), and side \(r = 13\). Find the exact value of \(\cos P\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Apply the Law of Cosines for angle \(P\): \[ p^2 = q^2 + r^2 - 2qr\cos P \implies \cos P = \frac{q^2 + r^2 - p^2}{2qr}. \]

Step 2: Substitute given side lengths: \[ \cos P = \frac{11^2 + 13^2 - 8^2}{2(11)(13)} = \frac{121 + 169 - 64}{286} = \frac{226}{286} = \mathbf{\frac{113}{143}} \approx 0.7902. \]

question.en: A triangle has side lengths \(a = 5\), \(b = 6\), and \(c = 7\). Use Heron's formula to compute its exact area.

solution.en:
Step 1: Compute semi-perimeter \(s\): \[ s = \frac{a + b + c}{2} = \frac{5 + 6 + 7}{2} = \frac{18}{2} = 9. \]

Step 2: Apply Heron's formula: \[ \text{Area} = \sqrt{s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)} = \sqrt{9(9 - 5)(9 - 6)(9 - 7)} = \sqrt{9(4)(3)(2)} = \sqrt{216} = \mathbf{6\sqrt{6}} \approx 14.70. \]
